pull.title: rpc: reset id and version per batch element
pull.body:
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` uses one request object for the whole batch. `parse()` throws on a non-object before it resets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I reset both fields at the top of `parse()`, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.

Reviewed and tested, looks good to me.

Small nit: the existing m_json_version reset before the jsonrpc check is now redundant and could be removed.

concept ACK

This is a reasonable follow up to #27101 and fixes something we missed from the jsonrpc 2.0 spec that could confuse consumers of the interface expecting unique IDs in batch responses.

Done: I removed the second `m_json_version` reset and simplified the test's asserts. The batch case now checks the valid reply, then that the error reply has another id and no `jsonrpc` field, which fails if the version reset stays where it was; the notification case checks that the error reply is there.

@AndreaDiazCorreia, the removed reset is the one from your nit; would you mind taking another look at 2ab7c47f60?

committer Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net> 1793743587 +0100

rpc: reset id and version per batch element

In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error
reply with the id and version of the element before it. A client that
matches replies by id can take that error for the result of the
previous call. If the previous element was a 2.0 notification, the
error is dropped.

I reset both at the start of JSONRPCRequest::parse(). The functional
test covers the two cases.
